{"body":"## Reviewer brief

**Result:** `pnpm --dir apps/obsidian lint:scanner` runs the ESLint config the Obsidian community directory uses to scan every release. Errors block a submission; warnings don't. The blocking rules also show in the editor, and CI fails when a PR adds a line that breaks one. No source files change.

**Why now:** our v1.7.0 scan reported errors we couldn't see locally. Both reproduce with this config at the exact file and line (`useSchemaSelection.ts:117`, `tagNodeHandler.ts:120`).

**Review focus:**

- `packages/eslint-config/obsidian-scanner.upstream.js` is vendored verbatim (MIT) from [obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows](https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows/blob/8167caed39664214d82c86fdfa32e06d8d55f61d/src/lint.ts#L544-L697): the exact output of its `buildScannerEslintConfig()` at commit `8167cae`. Review that it matches upstream rather than reading it line by line. It's in `.prettierignore` so it stays diffable.
- `apps/obsidian/eslint.config.mjs`, the config editors read, derives the blocking rules from the vendored file instead of listing them: every rule at `error`, the plugin instances that define them, and the scanner's ignores, so `scripts/` and tests stay out as they do in the real scan. Re-vendoring a newer upstream updates the editor with no second edit.
- `lint:scanner` runs as a separate config and process because `@repo/eslint-config` loads `eslint-plugin-only-warn`, which patches ESLint on import and forces every rule to `warn`. The main config can therefore only report blockers as warnings, so `.vscode/settings.json` renders them as errors in the editor.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` runs `lint:scanner` through reviewdog with `-filter-mode=added` and `-fail-level=error`, matching `lint-changed-files`.

**Risk and follow-up:**

- The official scan reported 67 ESLint errors at `256ff3be`, this branch's verification base. CI reports existing findings without blocking. Clearing them is ENG-2341, which has since merged to main.
- **Outside ESLint, the official scan reports a manifest error:** `manifest-id-banned-word`, because plugin ID `@discourse-graph/obsidian` contains "obsidian". Changing an existing plugin's ID breaks installs, so this needs a decision separate from this PR.

- The scanner's stylelint pass isn't mirrored yet; the official run reports 39 stylelint warnings and no stylelint errors on our CSS. Follow-up.
- Our v1.7.0 directory scan reported "Source review dependency installation failed", a [known scanner limitation with pnpm workspaces](https://forum.obsidian.md/t/bug-plugin-scorecard-linter-cannot-resolve-internal-deps-in-monorepos/116176), so `.tsx` files were never scanned there. **Review branch** on the directory entry stays the only real check.
- 10 files is above the five-file guideline. The diff is 268 lines excluding the lockfile, and 151 of those are the vendored config.

**Against Obsidian's own scanner code.** I ran the `obsidian-workflows` action itself (`dist/index.js` at `8167cae`, `scanner-lint: true`, `strict: true`) and this PR's `lint:scanner` on a clean checkout of `256ff3be`:

| Official action, strict | 67 | 111 |
| This PR's `lint:scanner` | 68 | 110 |

176 of 178 findings match by file, line, column, rule, and severity. The two differences:

- `postcss.config.js`: both runs hit the same parse failure. The action reports it as a notice and raw ESLint as an error. It's at line 0, so it never lands on an added line and CI is unaffected.
- `fileChangeListener.ts:239`: the action reports one `no-unnecessary-type-assertion` warning that this PR doesn't. The cause is the TypeScript version: the action doesn't pin TypeScript, so npm resolves typescript-eslint's peer to 6.0.3, while this PR uses the repo's 5.5.4. A 2×2 run (typescript-eslint 8.61.1/8.67.0 × TypeScript 5.5.4/6.0.3) reports the warning exactly when TypeScript is 6.0.3. Warning-level, so it doesn't block.

- The vendored file is byte-identical to upstream's generator output, and the commit hook leaves it unchanged.

content.text:
I verified the contested facts rather than just summarizing the thread. Two findings change the shape of the argument, so I'll lead with those.

## Two things that reframe the meeting

**1. `strict: false` is worse than Michael's reading and worse than you argued.** You said it flattens errors into warnings. It's actually destructive: `applyEnforcement` in `src/main.ts:23-46` rewrites the finding *before* anything is reported, and only the rewritten array reaches the annotations and the step summary. There is no JSON/SARIF output and no counts output — only `type`, `validation-passed`, `release-url`. So the pre-downgrade severity survives nowhere. Your objection is correct; you now have the code to prove it instead of asserting it.

**2. But your "the 65 will block the next release" claim is the one without evidence.** Obsidian's own docs say the submission gate is one-time: *"You only need to submit the initial version of your plugin. After your plugin has been published, users can download new releases from GitHub directly from within Obsidian."* `community-plugins.json` holds only id/name/author/description/repo — no version field, no per-release approval. The client reads the version from our repo's `manifest.json` and fetches the matching GitHub release. The install-block sentence ("won't be installable until any errors from the automated review are resolved") sits under Step 4 of the *initial* submission flow. No public doc says it re-arms per release on a live entry. The only documented lever against a published plugin is archiving the entry.

This is exactly what Michael has been asking for three times, and the honest answer is that neither of you can establish it from public docs. It's login-gated.

## The four questions

**Q1 — What evidence establishes which findings actually block our published plugin?**

Separate three gates that have been treated as one:

| Gate | Can it stop a release reaching users? |
|---|---|
| Our CI running the action | No. The directory never reads it. |
| The directory scorecard on a live entry | No documented mechanism. Unconfirmed. |
| Human/automated review at first submission | Yes — but spent in our case. |

The action's own step summary says it outright: *"Passing here does not guarantee directory acceptance."*

Concrete way to settle it before deciding anything else: our entry has **Review branch → Run preview scan**, which scans a branch/tag/SHA with no release. Run it on current `main` and read the scorecard. That gives the authoritative error/warning split on the real published artifact, which is the evidence neither of you has. If it's still ambiguous, ask Obsidian directly.

**Q2 — Official action, drop editor parity, remove the copied config?**

My read: yes to dropping the copied config, but not by putting the action in this repo. The action operates on `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` only — there is no input to point it at a subdirectory, so it can't cleanly target `apps/obsidian` in a Turborepo. Running it in the mirror repo `discourse-graph-obsidian` puts it exactly where the directory actually scans, on the artifact that actually ships. That removes the vendored file, removes the monorepo mismatch, and makes the check meaningful.

Dropping exact editor parity is fine — you've both already agreed. Keep `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd` locally at its own severities for editor feedback.

**Q3 — Should existing findings block adoption?**

They shouldn't, and the strict/non-strict framing is a false binary. Run the action with `strict: true` in a **non-blocking** job (`continue-on-error`) and you keep the full error/warning distinction while nothing is gated on the backlog. Then your existing `lint-changed-files` pattern (`-filter-mode=added`) catches new violations. That gets Michael his maintained upstream config and you your severity signal, without fixing 65 things first.

Worth raising as a risk: forum thread 116176 is still open with no staff reply. In a pnpm monorepo the scanner lints with unresolved workspace types and emits `@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-*` noise. Those map to `warn`, so they wouldn't fail even under strict — but it's a live upstream bug and an argument for running in the mirror rather than here.

**Q4 — What proves the scan covered `.ts` and `.tsx`, and how do we fail on incomplete coverage?**

The action cannot prove it, and this is its sharpest weakness:

- `validation-passed` is computed purely from `status === 'failed' && severity === 'error'`. Inconclusive and skipped never touch it.
- A summary reading **"Inconclusive"** still emits `validation-passed: true` and exit 0.

Almost, but one correction: the store scanner never sees the monorepo. It only scans the published copy, [discourse-graph-obsidian](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph-obsidian), and that copy has no way to get the shared config.

## In simple terms

TypeScript has to be told how to read JSX, the HTML-like syntax inside `.tsx` files. That setting is `jsx`, and in our code it lives in one place only:

- [react-library.json:5](packages/typescript-config/react-library.json:5) contains `"jsx": "react-jsx"`.
- Our plugin's [tsconfig.json:2](apps/obsidian/tsconfig.json:2) doesn't set `jsx` itself. It only says "start from that shared file": `"extends": "@repo/typescript-config/react-library.json"`.

So whether `.tsx` files can be read depends on whether that shared file can be found.

## Why our CI finds it and the store doesn't

**In the monorepo (our CI and your laptop):**
- [apps/obsidian/package.json:24](apps/obsidian/package.json:24) lists `"@repo/typescript-config": "workspace:*"`.
- `pnpm install` turns that into a shortcut (a symlink) on disk. You have it: `apps/obsidian/node_modules/@repo/typescript-config → packages/typescript-config`.
- The `extends` resolves, `jsx` is set, the `.tsx` files get read, and all ~65 errors show up.

**In the published copy (what the store scans):**
- [publish.ts:408-434](apps/obsidian/scripts/publish.ts:408) copies the plugin and removes every `workspace:` dependency. Its comment says why: *"The community review runs npm install with no lockfile, so pnpm-only specifiers fail."*
- The mirror's `package.json` therefore has no `@repo/typescript-config`, and the package isn't on npm, so no install can supply it.
- The mirror's `tsconfig.json` is still an exact copy of ours, `extends` line included. It points at a file that doesn't exist there.

In one line: **our CI has the symlink and the store doesn't.** Same code, same tsconfig, but the shared file only exists inside the monorepo.

The `include: ["**/*.ts"]` setting also plays a part. It only lists `.ts` files directly; `.tsx` files get pulled in because `.ts` files import them. That's why `.tsx` files get linted in CI even though `include` never names them. You described this in your [Nov 2 comment](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1328#issuecomment-6580132197).

## What's proven and what isn't

**Checked against the code just now:**
- `jsx` is set only in the shared file.
- The mirror's tsconfig extends that file.
- The mirror's `package.json` doesn't include it.
- `publish.ts` removes it on purpose.
- The monorepo has the symlink.

**Measured earlier, by you:** with a broken install, errors went from 65 to 1, and 56 `.tsx` files were skipped as notices. In the action's code, a file ESLint can't parse becomes `eslint-execution-failure`, which is only a notice and never fails the run (`src/lint.ts:294-318` at `8167cae`).

**Not proven:** that the missing `jsx` setting is what causes the skip. I tried to clone the mirror and run the scan here, but the command was declined. There's also a timing question. ENG-2341 ([#1499](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1499), merged Sept 29) added the `package.json` cleanup, so `npm install` may now succeed on the mirror (currently 1.8.0). If it does, the missing shared config is the only blocker left. The latest scorecard for 1.8.0 would show which: whether it still says "Source review dependency installation failed", and whether any `.tsx` findings appear.

## What this means for the fix

Adding `**/*.tsx` to `include` won't change the store scan, because the `extends` stays broken either way. The fix is in `publish.ts`: write a tsconfig into the mirror that has the shared settings copied in (including `jsx`) instead of the `extends` line. The mirror's `eslint.config.mjs` has the same problem, since it imports `@repo/eslint-config`. Once both are self-contained, the store should start linting the `.tsx` files, and the ~65 errors will show up there too.

content.text:
The action never looks at a diff at all. I searched the source we saved from `8167cae` and none of it reads a base branch, a merge-base or a list of changed files. Its seven inputs (`type`, `mode`, `build`, `lint`, `scanner-lint`, `strict`, `node-version`) have no option for one either. It always checks the whole repo.

## Why it's built that way

The README states the purpose in one line: *"Matches the community directory's validation and scanner expectations so your submissions pass on the first try."*

The directory judges a **whole release**, not a change. So the question the action is built to answer is "would this release pass?", and you can only answer that by checking everything. A changed-line filter answers a different question: "did this PR make things worse?" Obsidian built a release predictor, not a code-review gate.

Two things in the code back this up:
- **Most of its checks aren't about lines at all.** Manifest validity, release assets, the build, dependency checks and the registry lookup are all whole-project facts. A line filter only makes sense for lint findings.
- **It has no output a filter could use.** The only outputs are `type`, `validation-passed` and `release-url`. There's no per-finding JSON, so you can't even filter its results afterwards without scraping the step summary.

That's my reading of the design. The README doesn't say "we chose not to add a filter", but everything in it points at release validation.

## What it means for the PR debate

If you want "only fail on new violations", the action can't do it. You have to run ESLint yourself and filter with something like reviewdog `-filter-mode=added`, which is what your `obsidian-scanner-lint` job does.

Michael's [Nov 4 review](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1328) actually needs this too. His plan is the action with `strict: true` after the backlog is fixed, *plus* "a separate CI lint check (possibly scoped to changed lines)". That separate check has to get the scanner's rules and severities from somewhere. There are two options:
- **The official plugin's `recommended` preset:** maintained upstream, but its severities aren't the scanner's. The scanner downgrades everything to warning and then re-escalates a specific list, so the two don't match.
- **The scanner's generated config:** the right severities, but that's the file you vendored.

So the real question for the meeting isn't "action or copied config". It's where the changed-lines check gets its rules from, because both plans need one.

They come from your official-action run in the [PR thread](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1328#issuecomment-6003442469) (strict mode, base `256ff3be`, August): **67 ESLint errors, 64 in `.tsx` and 3 in `.ts`**. ENG-2341 fixed 2 of the 3 `.ts` ones. I checked every `.tsx` finding against current `main` and all of them are still there. I couldn't rerun the scanner on today's `main`, because `lint:scanner` only exists on the PR branch, so code added since August may have changed the total slightly.

They're concentrated: 4 canvas files hold 57 of the 67, and [relationUtils.tsx](apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/relationUtils.tsx) alone has 31.

## The four groups

**1. Disable comments written the wrong way: 38 errors, about 2 hours**

| Rule | Count | What it wants |
|---|---|---|
| `eslint-comments/require-description` | 25 | Add `-- reason` after every `eslint-disable` |
| `eslint-comments/disable-enable-pair` | 12 | A whole-file disable needs a matching `eslint-enable` |
| `eslint-comments/no-restricted-disable` | 1 | You may not disable `no-explicit-any` at all |

Most of these come from the top of [relationUtils.tsx:1-15](apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/relationUtils.tsx:1), which has 12 whole-file disable comments. Each one triggers 2 errors, so 12 lines produce 24. The fix is mechanical: delete the ones that no longer suppress anything, then add reasons and closing comments to the rest. The banned `no-explicit-any` disable is cheap to remove because the file only has 2 `any`s.

These are only errors because the scanner exempts `eslint-comments/*` from its "downgrade everything to warning" step.

**2. Disable comments naming rules the scanner doesn't load: 13 errors, about half a day, and a config conflict**

| Rule named in the comment | Count | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `preferArrows/prefer-arrow-functions` | 6 | Mostly [DiscourseRelationBinding.tsx](apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/shapes/DiscourseRelationBinding.tsx:192) |
| `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` | 4 | NodeShape, RelationshipSection, relationUtils, useSchemaSelection |
| `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` | 3 | [DiscourseRelationShape.tsx:829, 886](apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/shapes/DiscourseRelationShape.tsx:829), relationUtils |

The error message is *"Definition for rule '…' was not found."* Our own lint config loads these plugins and the scanner's doesn't. So a comment that **our** lint needs is an error to **the scanner**. Deleting the comment breaks `pnpm lint`, and keeping it fails the scan. The only fix that satisfies both is changing the code so no disable comment is needed:
- **prefer-arrow (6):** turn the functions into arrow functions. Easy.
- **exhaustive-deps (4):** each needs a real look at the hook's dependencies.
- **rules-of-hooks (3):** the hard one. These are hooks called inside tldraw shape methods, so the fix probably means moving that code into a proper component, and it needs canvas testing.

One leftover from ENG-2341: [useSchemaSelection.ts:117](apps/obsidian/src/components/useSchemaSelection.ts:117) now has a `-- reason`, but it still names `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`. By this logic the "rule not found" half of that finding probably still fails the scan. I haven't confirmed that by running the scanner.

**3. Inline styles: 15 errors, about half a day plus testing**

All `obsidianmd/no-static-styles-assignment`:
- **[DiscourseToolPanel.tsx:164-189](apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/DiscourseToolPanel.tsx:164), 11:** the drag-preview image. Fixed values move to a CSS class. The moving position (`transform`) is already allowed; the rule only flags fixed values.
- **[ModifyNodeModal.tsx:170, 204](apps/obsidian/src/components/ModifyNodeModal.tsx:170), 2:** popover placement and textarea auto-height. These change at runtime, so they use Obsidian's `setCssProps`.
- **[relationUtils.tsx:1466, 1470](apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/relationUtils.tsx:1466), 2:** a hide-then-show trick on tldraw's HTML layer that forces a re-render. Switching it to a class toggle should work, but it's timing-sensitive, so it needs a canvas check.

Low risk to write; the time goes into checking drag-and-drop and the modal by hand.

**4. Already fixed: 1 error**

[tagNodeHandler.ts:120](apps/obsidian/src/utils/tagNodeHandler.ts:120), `no-forbidden-elements` (creating a `<style>` element). ENG-2341 removed it.

## Effort

| Group | Errors | Effort | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Comment format | 38 | ~2 h | None |
| Rules the scanner doesn't load | 13 | ~0.5 day | rules-of-hooks touches canvas |
| Inline styles | 15 | ~0.5 day + testing | Drag preview, modal, layer re-render |
| Already fixed | 1 | — | — |

That's about **1.5 to 2.5 days**, including canvas and modal checks. It splits naturally into two PRs: a mechanical one for group 1 plus the arrow-function part of group 2, then a behaviour one for the hooks and styles that needs testing.

## For the meeting

- **Fixing them first, as Michael proposes, is affordable.** It's days, not weeks, and about half of it is one afternoon of editing comments.
- **Group 2 is worth raising in its own right.** Those 13 errors exist because our lint config and the scanner's disagree about which rules exist. Whatever CI setup you agree on has to deal with that, or new disable comments will keep producing these errors.

Okay, I think can you create a draft PR that addresses all of these and group them in a way that makes it easy to review? If this draft PR ended up being too big, then maybe it makes sense to split it into 4 different PRs. Feel free to create a linear ticket first to track all these works.

# DG Create Engineering Ticket

Create an Engineering ticket that another engineer can understand and implement without rediscovering its intent or scope.

Use `$dg-engineering-writing-style` when available. It is in the repository's `./.agents/skills` folder.

## Canonical template

The canonical Linear template is [General Engineering Task](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/new?template=6ca39698-3bce-449a-992e-059f0334e15b). Keep this link only as a reference in this skill. Never add it to a created ticket.

Use this exact template as the drafting checklist:

```markdown
## Problem

- What accepted user, developer, or project need does this address?
- Why does it need to be solved now?

## Solution

- What is the smallest change that solves the problem?

## Done When

- Describe how success is verified (behavioral or technical).
- Remember: Make only the smallest change needed to solve the problem.
- Remember: **Stay within the defined scope, or communicate any scope increase**

## Out of Scope

- (Optional) What adjacent cases, abstractions, or future work are explicitly not included?
- Link follow-up tickets where applicable

## Notes

- Additional Context, Blockers, dependencies, or follow-up actions.
```

Every bullet above is placeholder guidance. Replace or remove every placeholder before presenting a draft or creating a ticket. Keep all five headings, leaving `Out of Scope` or `Notes` empty when nothing useful applies. Use 1–3 short bullets per section unless the ticket is genuinely complex.

## Agent provenance and human review

Always use the Engineering team. This skill never creates or redirects to Feedback.

- Create every agent-created ticket in the existing `Ticket Draft` status with exactly one existing workspace provenance label from the `Created by` group. The label records provenance and stays after approval.
- Select the label from the creating agent's known identity: `Created by Claude` for Claude, `Created by Codex` for Codex, or `Created by LLM` for any other agent or when its identity cannot be determined. Do not infer agent identity from the Linear account, ticket topic, or skill name. Do not use `Created by LLM` as a substitute when the correct agent-specific label is missing.
- `Ticket Draft` is in the Backlog category and means human ticket review is pending; it does not authorize implementation. The existing `Draft` status belongs to the Started category and is used by the PR workflow. Do not use it for ticket review or change its automation.
- In `Notes`, record `Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket` and any other creation skills actually used. Skill attribution is provenance, not evidence that the ticket meets the standards.
- The human who asked the agent to create the ticket checks intent against the source request, scope and exclusions, verifiable acceptance criteria, and the canonical template and engineering writing standards. Keep the ticket in `Ticket Draft` while changes are needed.
- Human approval moves the ticket to `Backlog` when the problem and fix are agreed and implementation needs no further product or solution decisions. Use `Triage` when implementation is likely within six months but decisions remain. Keep idea-stage Engineering requests in Engineering.
- The human's move from `Ticket Draft` to `Triage` or `Backlog` records sign-off. An agent may make that move only after explicit human approval of the completed ticket and destination. A request to create a ticket is not approval of its generated contents. Keep the provenance label and skill attribution.

## Project selection

Resolve the project in this order:

1. Use the project explicitly named by the user.
2. Use a clearly relevant active project from the current work context.
3. For Obsidian work with no relevant project, leave the project empty and apply the existing `Obsidian plugin` label. Do not use `Obsidian Discourse Graphs plugin assorted tasks`; the Obsidian queue picks up unprojected issues by label (see DIS-617).
4. For Roam work, use `Roam Discourse Graph plugin assorted tasks`.
5. Otherwise, use `Engineering Ops assorted tasks`.

Any project you select must exist, not be completed, canceled, archived, or trashed, and include the Engineering team. Never create a project. If a user-specified project is missing, ambiguous, or inactive, ask the user for another project instead of silently substituting one. Obsidian tickets that do belong to a real project still use that project, plus the `Obsidian plugin` label.

## Labels and optional fields

- Inspect existing issue labels and apply every clearly relevant label. Always apply `Obsidian plugin` to Obsidian work, since it is how unprojected Obsidian tickets reach the queue.
- Never create a label or guess an uncertain label.
- Missing or uncertain optional labels do not block creation. If `Ticket Draft`, the required provenance label, or `Obsidian plugin` for Obsidian work is missing or ambiguous, return the prepared draft and report the configuration gap instead of creating an unmarked ticket or substituting a status.
- Set priority only when the user or context makes it clear and useful.
- Do not set a cycle or release. CI/CD handles releases.

## Create or draft

Draft without changing Linear when the user asks for a draft, review, or rewrite. Create the ticket without an additional confirmation when the user explicitly asks to create it.

Before creation, resolve the current Engineering statuses, selected project, and existing labels. Create the issue once with its title, completed description (including skill attribution), `Ticket Draft` status, project (omitted for unprojected Obsidian work), provenance and relevant labels, and justified priority. If the result is ambiguous, search for the issue before retrying so a transient failure does not create a duplicate.

Read the created issue back and verify its status, labels, and attribution. For unprojected Obsidian work, confirm the project is empty and `Obsidian plugin` is applied. Report any mismatch instead of claiming successful routing. Return the issue identifier, title, status, project, and link, and say that human review is pending. Include the generated branch name when Linear returns one. Do not restate the full description unless the user asks.

# Clear the Obsidian scanner's 65 blocking ESLint errors

## Context

Obsidian's directory scanner (obsidian-workflows `8167cae`) reports **65 blocking ESLint errors** in `apps/obsidian`. 64 are in `.tsx` files. I measured this on current `main`. The real store scan doesn't see them yet, because the mirror repo's `tsconfig.json` extends an unpublished `@repo/typescript-config`. Once that's fixed, the errors will show up there. Michael's Nov 4 review on PR #1328 asks for these to be fixed before adopting the official action. This plan delivers that fix.

Current breakdown (same rule groups as the August trace):

| Group | Errors | Kind of change |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Directive comment format (`require-description`, `disable-enable-pair`, `no-restricted-disable`) | 37 | Comments only |
| 2. Directives naming rules the scanner doesn't load (`preferArrows` 6, `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` 4, `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` 3) | 13 | Code changes |
| 3. `obsidianmd/no-static-styles-assignment` | 15 | Code + CSS |

There's also one `postcss.config.js` parse failure, which the official action reports as a notice, not an error. It's out of scope.

## Step 0: Ticket and worktree

- Create one Engineering ticket with `dg-create-engineering-ticket`: status `Ticket Draft`, label `Created by Claude` + `Obsidian plugin` + `Bug`, no project (unprojected Obsidian work, per the skill), related to ENG-1832 and ENG-2341. Title: "Fix the Obsidian scanner's blocking ESLint errors". Done When: the scanner config reports 0 errors in `apps/obsidian`, repo lint adds no warnings on changed lines, and canvas and modal behaviour is unchanged. Out of scope: CI adoption (ENG-1832), the mirror tsconfig fix, the 106 scanner warnings, the stylelint warnings.
- Create a worktree from `origin/main` using Linear's branch name, under `.claude/worktrees/`, then run `pnpm install`.

**Scanner harness (verification only, never committed):** `lint:scanner` only exists on the ENG-1832 branch. To get counts, run that worktree's ESLint and config against the new worktree:
```
cd <new-worktree>/apps/obsidian
<eng-1832-worktree>/apps/obsidian/node_modules/.bin/eslint . \
  --config <eng-1832-worktree>/apps/obsidian/eslint.config.scanner.mjs \
  --no-config-lookup --format json -o <scratchpad>/scan.json
```
This gave 65 on `main`. Rerun it after every group.

## Group 1 — directive comments (commit 1, no behaviour change)

- **`relationUtils.tsx:1-15` header** (27 of the 37): this file is ported from tldraw's arrow code and has 12 whole-file disables. For each one, delete it and check whether anything fires. Drop the ones that no longer suppress anything. Keep the rest with a `-- reason`, plus a matching `/* eslint-enable */` at the end of the file.
- **Remove the `no-explicit-any` disable** (it's on the scanner's restricted list). The file has only 2 `any`s; type them properly or use `unknown`.
- **Add `-- reason` to every remaining next-line disable** that names a rule the scanner loads, e.g. `DiscourseRelationBinding.tsx:278`, `TldrawView.tsx:66`. Where the reason shows the disable is no longer needed, fix the code instead.
- Leave the `react-hooks/*` and `preferArrows/*` directive lines alone. Group 2 deletes them, so editing them here would only create churn.

## Group 2 — rules the scanner doesn't load (commit 2)

The constraint: our config loads `react-hooks` and `prefer-arrow-functions`, and the scanner doesn't. **A directive naming either is always an error to the scanner.** Each site needs a fix that doesn't use a directive:

- **`preferArrows` (5 next-line sites in `DiscourseRelationBinding.tsx`):** convert those `function` declarations to `const` arrows. First check each one isn't called before its definition at module load (hoisting).
- **`preferArrows` file-wide in `relationUtils.tsx`:** the file has 69 `function` declarations. Converting all of them is scope creep in a ported file. Instead, move the suppression into `apps/obsidian/eslint.config.mjs` as a file-scoped override (`files: ["src/components/canvas/utils/relationUtils.tsx"]`, prefer-arrow off, with a one-line comment). The scanner never reads our config, so this can't trigger "rule not found".
- **`rules-of-hooks`:**
  - `DiscourseRelationShape.tsx:829`: the directive sits above a commented-out line. Delete both.
  - `DiscourseRelationShape.tsx:886`, `indicator()` calls `useIsEditing`: replace it with a direct `this.editor.getEditingShapeId() === shape.id`. tldraw renders `indicator` inside a tracked component, so reading the signal directly stays reactive.
  - `relationUtils.tsx:558`: `props.theme ?? useDefaultColorTheme()` calls the hook conditionally. Call it unconditionally, then fall back. This also lets the file-wide `rules-of-hooks` disable go, so the rule protects this file again.
- **`exhaustive-deps` (4):**
  - `useSchemaSelection.ts:117` (reset only on `resetKey`): use React's "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern. Keep `prevResetKey` in state and compare during render. No effect, no directive.
  - `RelationshipSection.tsx:100`: the effect only sets derived state. Turn it into a `useMemo` with complete deps, or add the missing dep if that's the only gap.
  - `DiscourseNodeShape.tsx:384`: read the full effect and add the missing deps if they're stable. If they aren't, read the volatile values through a ref.
  - `relationUtils.tsx:1890` (Safari render-index memo keyed on `shape`, also tldraw-ported): replace it with a ref that bumps the index when `shape` identity changes, so the hook's deps are honest.

## Group 3 — static inline styles (commit 3)

The rule only flags **static** values. Dynamic ones like `transform: translate(${…})` and `top: ${rect.bottom}px` already pass, so only the static assignments change:

- **`DiscourseToolPanel.tsx:164-189`** (drag-preview image, 11): put the static styles (`position: fixed`, `pointer-events: none`, `left/top: 0`, 50×50, flex centering) in one class in `styles.css`. Use Obsidian's `el.show()`/`el.hide()` for the visibility toggles. Keep the dynamic `transform`.
- **`ModifyNodeModal.tsx:170`:** add `position: fixed` to the popover's `className`. The dynamic `top/left/width` stay.
- **`ModifyNodeModal.tsx:204`:** the `height = "auto"` reset before measuring `scrollHeight` → use `el.setCssStyles({ height: "auto" })`. There's precedent for the Obsidian helpers in `src/utils/measureNodeText.ts:39`.
- **`relationUtils.tsx:1466, 1470`** (hide/show tldraw's HTML layer to force a pattern re-render): use `htmlLayer.hide()` / `htmlLayer.show()`.

Run the scanner harness to confirm the Obsidian helpers aren't flagged too. If one is, fall back to a class toggle.

## PR shape

Build everything on one branch, **one commit per group**. Then measure the diff:
- **Under ~400 lines excluding tests:** one draft PR, with the reviewer brief pointing to the three commits (the first is comments only; the other two change behaviour and come with test steps).
- **Over that:** split into stacked draft PRs in the same order (1 → 2 → 3). All three touch the `relationUtils.tsx` header, so stacking avoids conflicts.

My estimate is about 150-250 lines, so probably one PR.

## Verification

1. **Scanner harness:** 0 errors (only the `postcss.config.js` notice remains), and the warning count doesn't go up.
2. **Repo checks:** `pnpm --filter @discourse-graphs/obsidian lint`, `check-types`, `test` (Vitest). Lint must show no new warnings on changed lines, since `lint-changed-files` fails on warnings.
3. **Live Obsidian check** (lease a vault with `obsidian-vault`, drive with `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify`), with a screenshot for each:
   - Drag a node type from the Discourse tool panel onto the canvas: the preview follows the cursor, hides over the panel, and disappears on drop.
   - Draw a relation arrow and edit its label: the indicator updates while editing (the `useIsEditing` change).
   - Arrows with pattern fill render, and the HTML-layer re-render still happens (`hide`/`show`).
   - Node shape resizes when the file's content or title changes (`DiscourseNodeShape` deps).
   - Modify Node modal: the search popover sits under the title input, and the title textarea grows as you type.
   - Relationship section: compatible node types update when you change relation type. The schema-selection reset still fires on `resetKey`.
4. **Hand-test pause:** before opening the PR, give Trang exact steps for those six checks to try by hand.
5. **Cross-check (optional):** rerun Obsidian's own action at `8167cae` in strict mode, using the reproduction from the ENG-1832 thread, and confirm 0 ESLint errors.
6. **Pre-PR:** invoke `scope-check`, `dg-pr-adherence-check` and `dg-delegated-full-review` on the final head. Write the PR body file first, from `.github/pull_request_template.md`, then run `gh pr create --draft`.

## Critical files

- `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/relationUtils.tsx` (31 of the errors)
- `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/shapes/DiscourseRelationBinding.tsx`, `DiscourseRelationShape.tsx`, `DiscourseNodeShape.tsx`
- `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/DiscourseToolPanel.tsx`, `apps/obsidian/src/components/ModifyNodeModal.tsx`
- `apps/obsidian/src/components/RelationshipSection.tsx`, `apps/obsidian/src/components/useSchemaSelection.ts`
- `apps/obsidian/eslint.config.mjs` (one file-scoped prefer-arrow override), `apps/obsidian/styles.css` (drag-preview class)

  - `relationUtils.tsx:558`: `props.theme ?? useDefaultColorTheme()` calls the hook conditionally. Call it unconditionally, then fall back. This also lets the file-wide `rules-of-hooks` disable go, so the rule protects this file again.
- **`exhaustive-deps` (4):**
  - `useSchemaSelection.ts:117` (reset only on `resetKey`): use React's "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern. Keep `prevResetKey` in state and compare during render. No effect, no directive.
  - `RelationshipSection.tsx:100`: the effect only sets derived state. Turn it into a `useMemo` with complete deps, or add the missing dep if that's the only gap.
  - `DiscourseNodeShape.tsx:384`: the effect reads `shape.props.size` and `fontFamily` (:354-355) but doesn't list them as deps. Adding them would make nodes resize on a style-panel change, which they don't do today. **Keep today's triggers exactly:** read `size`/`fontFamily` through a ref that updates every render, and list every other value in the deps. The missing resize on style change goes in the ticket's Notes as a possible follow-up, not this PR.
  - `relationUtils.tsx:1890` (Safari render-index memo keyed on `shape`, also tldraw-ported): replace it with a ref that bumps the index when `shape` identity changes, so the hook's deps are honest. On Chromium the index stays 0, as it does today.

This plan doesn't convert any `relationUtils` functions to arrows (the file-scoped override covers it), so nothing moves. Converting that one would crash the plugin on load.

## Group 3 — static inline styles (commit 3)

The rule only flags **static** values. Dynamic ones like `transform: translate(${…})` and `top: ${rect.bottom}px` already pass, so only the static assignments change:

- **`DiscourseToolPanel.tsx:164-189`** (drag-preview image, 11): put the static styles (`position: fixed`, `pointer-events: none`, `left/top: 0`, 50×50, flex centering) in one class in `styles.css`. Use Obsidian's `el.show()`/`el.hide()` for the visibility toggles. Keep the dynamic `transform`.

- **`ModifyNodeModal.tsx:204`:** the `height = "auto"` reset before measuring `scrollHeight` → use `el.setCssStyles({ height: "auto" })`. There's precedent for the Obsidian helpers in `src/utils/measureNodeText.ts:39`.

Build everything on one branch, **one commit per group**. Then measure the diff:
- **Under ~400 lines excluding tests:** one draft PR, with the reviewer brief pointing to the three commits (the first is comments only; the other two change behaviour and come with test steps).
- **Over that:** split into stacked draft PRs in the same order (1 → 2 → 3). All three touch the `relationUtils.tsx` header, so stacking avoids conflicts.

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.

input.description:
## Problem

- The Obsidian community directory scanner config (obsidian-workflows `8167cae`) reports 65 blocking ESLint errors in `apps/obsidian`. 64 are in `.tsx` files.
- The store scan doesn't see them yet: the mirror repo's `tsconfig.json` extends the unpublished `@repo/typescript-config`, so `.tsx` files never get linted. Once that's fixed, these errors appear in the directory scan.
- PR #1328 review (ENG-1832) asks for these errors to be fixed before we adopt the official action with `strict: true`.

## Solution

Fix the errors in three groups, one commit each:

- **Directive comments (37):** add `-- reason` descriptions, pair whole-file disables with `eslint-enable`, remove the banned `no-explicit-any` disable.
- **Directives naming rules the scanner doesn't load (13):** our config loads `react-hooks` and `prefer-arrow-functions`, and the scanner doesn't, so any directive naming them is an error. Replace each with a code fix (arrow functions, unconditional hooks, complete deps). Move the file-wide prefer-arrow suppression in the ported `relationUtils.tsx` into `apps/obsidian/eslint.config.mjs`.
- **Static inline styles (15, `obsidianmd/no-static-styles-assignment`):** move static values to CSS classes and use Obsidian's `show()`/`hide()`/`setCssStyles()`. Dynamic values stay.

## Done When

- The scanner config reports 0 ESLint errors in `apps/obsidian`. The `postcss.config.js` parse notice may remain.
- `pnpm lint` reports no new warnings on changed lines, and `check-types` and unit tests pass.
- Canvas, modal, sidebar and schema-dialog behaviour is unchanged, verified live in Obsidian against `main`. That covers the drag preview, ModifyNodeModal popover and auto-height, relation indicator, pattern fill, node load/resize, relation binding, relationship-section chips, and schema selection reset.

## Out of Scope

- Adopting the official action or a scanner CI job (ENG-1832).
- Making the mirror's `tsconfig.json` and `eslint.config.mjs` self-contained so the store scan lints `.tsx`.
- The ~106 scanner warnings, the stylelint warnings, and the `postcss.config.js` parse notice.

## Notes

- Error counts come from running the ENG-1832 branch's vendored scanner config against `main`. They match the official action's strict run in the PR #1328 thread.
- `DiscourseNodeShape`'s load effect reads `size` and `fontFamily` without listing them as deps, so nodes don't resize on a style-panel change. This ticket keeps that behaviour; changing it is a possible follow-up.
- Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style

Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/obsidian-vault

# Obsidian vault leases

One script, `~/.claude/skills/obsidian-vault/scripts/vault.mjs`, owns which worktree builds into which vault. Pass `--worktree <abs path>` on every call: the Bash cwd resets to the main repo between calls.

```sh
V=~/.claude/skills/obsidian-vault/scripts/vault.mjs
node $V status                          # every vault: free | idle | live, holder, watcher, CDP run
node $V dev --worktree <wt>             # claim + start the watcher (run_in_background)
node $V claim --worktree <wt>           # claim without starting anything
node $V claim --worktree <wt> --take <vault>   # only after the user approved it
node $V release --worktree <wt>         # stop this worktree's watcher, free its vault
node $V path --worktree <wt>            # print the leased plugin dir
```

## Pools

The registry at `~/.claude/state/obsidian-vaults.json` holds the pool and the leases. Edit its `vaults` array to add or remove vaults.

- `--db local` (default): dgDevVault, testVault, testVault2, Obsidian Vault. Normal dev work.
- `--db production`: testVault123. Use only when Trang asks to test against the prod database.

## The worktree's `.env` follows the lease

The lease is the source of truth, and `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env` mirrors it. Every claim writes `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH` and `SUPABASE_USE_DB` there and keeps the other lines. A plain `pnpm dev`, `vault.mjs dev` and `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` therefore all build into the same vault.

- A takeover clears the losing worktree's two keys, but only if they still point at that vault, so its next `pnpm dev` doesn't mirror anywhere.
- `release` clears them the same way.
- Don't hand-edit these keys. Claim or `--take` instead, or the `.env` and the registry disagree.
- A running watcher read `.env` at startup. If `claim` prints `restartWatcher`, restart `pnpm dev`.

## States

- **free**: no lease, nothing running. `claim` takes it silently.
- **idle**: leased to a worktree, but no watcher or CDP run. The session may still be alive and planning.
- **live**: an apps/obsidian `dev.ts` watcher mirrors into it (leased or not, found via `ps` + `lsof` cwd), or a `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` run holds its lock.

A worktree re-claiming gets its own vault back. A lease frees itself only when its worktree directory is gone, or on `release`.

## When `claim` or `dev` exits 2

# Obsidian CDP verify

## The one command

From the worktree root:

```sh
node ~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/run.mjs \
  --marker "<string only this change's bundle contains>" \
  --scenario path/to/scenarios.mjs [--scenario more.mjs] [--port 9222] [--skip-build] [--no-hide]
```

It runs claim → doctor → launch → deliver → scenarios → cleanup and prints the `last-run.json` path, the scenario matrix, and the `pr-evidence` args. Exit codes: 0 all pass, 1 failure, 2 no vault available or vault locked, 3 marker missing.

On exit 2 with `candidates`, follow the `obsidian-vault` skill: ask Trang which vault to take, then run `vault.mjs claim --take` and rerun.

Write scenario files in the session scratchpad, not the repo.

## Launch

- With no `--slot`, the vault is this worktree's `obsidian-vault` lease. `run.mjs` claims a free one if the worktree has no lease yet. This keeps the CDP run in the vault the worktree's watcher builds into.
- `--slot N` is a legacy override. It's a 1-based index into `OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_VAULTS` in `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env` and bypasses leases, so use it only when Trang names a slot.
- If Obsidian is running on the debug port, the script attaches.
- If it's running without the port, the script quits Obsidian and relaunches it with `--remote-debugging-port`. Trang approved this; the windows come back.
- If it isn't running, the script launches it with the port.
- It then opens the slot vault through `obsidian://open?path=` and waits for a page target where `.workspace` exists and `app.vault.adapter.basePath` matches the vault. The vault URL is skipped when that vault is already open.
- The run stays in the background: Obsidian is launched with `open -g` and hidden again whenever something raises it, which CDP input and screenshots do not need. Pass `--no-hide` to watch the run live. Obsidian is left alone if it was the frontmost app when the run started.
- It writes the lock `<vault>/.obsidian/dg-verify.lock` (`{pid, branch, startedAt}`) and releases it in `finally`.

## Doctor

`scripts/doctor.mjs [--slot N]` is read-only and prints JSON: the resolved vault, the lock and the Obsidian state. It exits 2 if the worktree has no lease, or if another live run holds the lock. A lock left by a dead pid is ignored.

## Deliver

`scripts/deliver.mjs --marker <str>` also runs on its own.

1. `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH=<slot plugin dir> tsx scripts/build.ts` runs once in `apps/obsidian`. It also writes `apps/obsidian/dist`, which is gitignored.
2. It greps the vault's `main.js` for `--marker` and fails if the marker is absent.
3. It reloads the plugin. The plugin id and folder are resolved from the manifests.
4. It greps again.
5. It warns about other worktrees' apps/obsidian `dev.ts` watchers that mirror into this vault. Your own worktree's watcher builds the same code, so it isn't flagged.

The harness also hashes `main.js` before and after the scenarios. If it changed, the run is marked invalid.

## Drive: scenario contract

A module's `export default` is one scenario or an array of them:

```js
export default {
  name: "Search modal renders",                 // matrix row + screenshot name
  input: "run open-node-search",                // matrix text
  expected: "modal with a textbox and footer",  // matrix text
  setup: async (ctx) => ({ /* state; snapshot anything you change */ }),  // optional
  run: async ({ client, json, vault }, state) => {
    await client.evaluate(`return app.commands.executeCommandById(${json(`${vault.pluginId}:open-node-search`)});`);
    await client.waitFor(`!!document.querySelector(".dg-node-search-modal [role=textbox]")`);
    return client.evaluate(`document.querySelectorAll(".dg-search-footer-action").length`);
  },
  expect: (actual, state) => ({ pass: actual > 0, actual: `${actual} footer actions` }),  // or a boolean
  teardown: async (ctx, state) => {},           // optional: restore what setup changed
};
```

- `ctx` has `client`, `vault` (`root`, `pluginId`, `pluginDir`), `branch`, `json`, `verifyPath(name)` and `writeNote(name, body)`. `writeNote` creates or overwrites `_verify/<branch>/<name>` and returns its path.
- `client` has `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `pressEscape`, `screenshot`, `reloadPlugin`, `clearModals` and `send` (raw CDP).
- The harness does these for you:
  - Before each scenario, it clears modals and restores the layout captured at the start of the run.
  - After `run`, it takes a screenshot.
  - A thrown error becomes a failing row.
- The worked example is `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` (ENG-2114, 3 scenarios).

## Evidence

- The artifacts go to `<worktree>/local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/<branch>/<runStamp>/`: `<n>-<slug>.png` and `last-run.json` (`results[]` of `{scenario, input, expected, actual, pass, screenshot}`).
- Paste the printed matrix into create-pr's Evidence section.
- Upload the screenshots with pr-evidence, using the printed args:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts --harness obsidian-cdp <printed args>
```

## Cleanup

- Cleanup dismisses modals (Escape, then force-removes leftover `.modal-container`), restores the baseline layout and releases the lock.
- **It never deletes folders or notes.** `_verify/<branch>/` persists, and reruns overwrite its notes.
- Scenarios that change vault or app settings must restore them in `teardown`.

## Gotchas

These are the ones the code can't handle for you.

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| Double-handled keypress | Pass `type` to `client.key` only through its loop. Never send your own `keyDown`. |
| `editor.hasFocus()` false while focus looks right | This can't be measured over CDP. Assert the consequence instead, e.g. the cursor moved past the inserted text. |
| File content assertion fails, editor looks right | Saves are debounced (about 2s). `waitFor` on `app.vault.read(...)`, and don't read once. |
| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found" | Every markdown leaf was detached. Use `getLeaf("tab")`. |
| Top-level `await` throws in `evaluate` | Bodies run in a plain function. Return an async IIFE or a promise chain. |
| `iterateRootLeaves` count caps at 2 | A truthy callback return stops the iteration. Use a block body `{ n++; }`. |
| Escape handler in a modal child never wins | Obsidian's modal scope runs first. Push a `Scope` with `app.keymap.pushScope`. |
| Styling CodeMirror spans disappears on focus or scroll | Use a CM6 decoration, not MutationObserver stamping. A widget's `ignoreEvent()` must stay `true` for clicks. |
| Selectors from an old ENG example don't match | The UI drifts. The node search input is now a contenteditable `[role=textbox]`, not an `<input>`. |
| Flaky failure that looks like a code bug | Trang may be using the app mid-run. Rerun before believing a single observation. |
| Timers stall, writes land minutes late | Focus emulation normally prevents this. If it recurs, check `document.visibilityState` and ask Trang to show the window. |
| zsh eats `${VAR}` in `node -e` | Write scenarios to `.mjs` files. |
| `waitFor` on an IIFE always times out | `evaluate` adds an outer `return` only when the code contains no `return`. An IIFE with an inner `return` evaluates to `undefined`, so write `return (() => { ... })()`. |
| A note written in `setup` is randomly missing from search results | Datacore indexes new files after the metadata cache, and the search loads through Datacore. After `writeNote`, also `waitFor` `dc.query("@page and exists(nodeTypeId)")` to include the path. |
